I can’t give a definitive “right now” answer because I don’t have access to live web/current‑info (the current‑information tool is offline) and you haven’t said which specific process or jurisdiction you mean. I won’t guess a current regulation without verifying.

To proceed I can either:
- Look it up as soon as you confirm I should and the current‑info tool is available, or
- Help you check it now by giving exact sources and search queries you can run.

If you want to check yourself, start with the authoritative sources for the relevant jurisdiction/sector (examples and suggested searches):

- United States (federal): Federal Register (federalregister.gov), Regulations.gov, and the relevant agency site (e.g., EPA, FDA, SEC). Search examples: “Federal Register new rule [topic] 2026”, “[agency name] final rule [topic] effective date”.
- United States (state): the state register or the state agency overseeing the topic (e.g., state environmental agency, state health department). Search: “[State name] administrative code [topic] new rule [year]”.
- European Union: EUR‑Lex / Official Journal (eur-lex.europa.eu). Search: “Commission delegated regulation [topic] 2026” or “Regulation (EU) [topic] Official Journal”.
- United Kingdom: legislation.gov.uk or gov.uk for consultations and guidance. Search: “[topic] statutory instrument 2026” or “[department] guidance [topic]”.
- Financial regulation: SEC (sec.gov), FINRA, ESMA. Search: “final rule [topic] SEC [year]” or “ESMA guidelines [topic]”.
- Health/medical: FDA (fda.gov), EMA (ema.europa.eu). Search: “FDA guidance [topic] 2026” or “EMA guideline [topic]”.

If you tell me:
- which process you mean (brief description), and
- the jurisdiction (country, state, EU/UK, or international), 

I’ll either give the exact lookup steps tailored to that case or (when you allow and tools are available) fetch and cite the authoritative regulation immediately. Which would you prefer?
